assessment: Using elegant cross-species biochemistry and genetic approaches, this paper describes the role of the ubiquitin adaptor protein LZTR1 in regulation of the RAS-related GTPase RIT1 as its principal substrate involved in the RASopathy, Noonan syndrome. Although this work does not fully rule out the involvement of canonical RAS isoforms in LZTR1-associated RASopathies in humans, the extensive genetic experiments in Drosophila and mouse presented here suggest that pathological phenotypes observed in LZTR1-linked RASopathy models are mediated primarily by its target RIT1, and not by canonical RAS isoforms.
